title: Engine world-space billboard primitive — `engine/render/billboard/` module for above-entity HUD elements
intent: S150 shipped Power-up HUD Layer 3 as a bottom-left HUD-side approximation because 'engine has no world-to-screen / billboard primitive yet' (S150 notes). The world-space-billboards-above-heads spec from GDP-2026-05-27-005 §3 Layer 3 was the original intent and a better player experience — opponent state telegraphs spatially, not flushed into the HUD corner. This story builds the missing primitive: an engine module `engine/render/billboard/` that any project can use to attach a 2D HUD-style element (icon / text / mini-row) to a 3D world position, billboarded toward the camera, with sane defaults for occlusion, scale-with-distance, and screen-space clamping. First consumer: re-implement opponent badges (S150) as billboards. Future consumers: nameplates in multiplayer, damage numbers, objective markers, Beacon World drone status, any project needing 'show this UI above that thing'.
rationale: Source: S150 sprint notes ('engine has no world-to-screen / billboard primitive yet ... filed as a deferred follow-up') + GDP-2026-05-27-005 §3 Layer 3 spec (world-space badges above bomber heads — design intent that S150 deferred). Mirrors the engine-first pattern set by the ragdoll module (GDP-2026-05-24-001) — when a game-side feature reveals a missing engine primitive, the primitive lives in the engine, projects consume it. Per CLAUDE.md 'engine ships only generic primitives + reusable systems'. World-space billboards are the textbook engine primitive: every character-driven 3D game in history needs them.
acceptanceHints: DIRECTORY: NEW `engine/render/billboard/`. Sits alongside the existing render primitives.
SCHEMA FILES (under `schemas/components/`):
billboard.schema.json — Billboard component {
contentKey: string,         // registered content builder (icon set, text style, custom)
contentPayload: object,     // builder-specific data — icons[] for icon-row builder, text+color for text builder, etc.
anchorEntityId: EntityId,   // entity whose Transform.position drives the billboard's world anchor
worldOffset?: [x, y, z],    // offset above anchor (default [0, 1.5, 0] — head height)
scaleMode?: 'fixed' | 'distance', // 'fixed' = constant screen size; 'distance' = shrink with distance (default 'fixed')
occlusionMode?: 'always-visible' | 'depth-tested', // default 'always-visible' (badges showing through walls — needed for the opponent-badges use case)
edgeClamp?: boolean,        // clamp to screen edge when anchor is off-screen (default false)
visibleWhenHidden?: boolean // continue rendering when anchor entity is despawned (default false — disappears with anchor)
billboard-content.schema.json — content registry types (icon-row, text-line, mini-stat-bar — extensible)
CONTENT BUILDER REGISTRY (engine/render/billboard/content-registry.ts):
registerBillboardContent(key: string, builder: (payload) => HTMLElement | OffscreenCanvas): void
Default builders shipped:
'icon-row' — payload: { icons: string[], colorTint?: string }, builder produces a horizontal row of mono cream silhouette icons
'text-line' — payload: { text: string, color?: string, size?: number }, builder produces a single line
'mini-stat-bar' — payload: { current: number, max: number, color: string }, builder produces a tiny bar (HP-style, but extensible)
Projects can register custom builders (e.g. kaboom: opponent-active-state-strip).
SYSTEMS (engine/render/billboard/):
createBillboardRenderSystem() — runs every frame (renderUpdate, not fixedUpdate). For each Billboard entity:
1. Look up the anchor entity's Transform; if missing AND visibleWhenHidden=false → hide the billboard's DOM element.
2. Project (anchor.position + worldOffset) to screen space using the renderer's camera.
3. If on-screen → position the DOM element at the projected (x,y); if off-screen AND edgeClamp=true → clamp to edge with directional indicator; if off-screen AND edgeClamp=false → hide.
4. Apply scale: 'fixed' = constant pixel size; 'distance' = scale by 1/distance with a min/max clamp.
5. Apply occlusion: 'always-visible' = always show; 'depth-tested' = raycast from camera to anchor; if blocked by world geometry, dim the element to 30% opacity.
Single system handles ALL billboards in the scene.
IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE:
Use HTML overlay (absolute-positioned DIVs over the Three.js canvas) for the actual rendering. This is the most flexible — projects can include any HTML in their content builder.
ALTERNATIVE: Three.js SpriteRenderer with HTML-rendered-to-canvas textures. More integrated, but slower to update on content change. Recommend HTML overlay for v1.
Both approaches are deterministic given the same camera + same Transform; pick HTML overlay.
DOCTOR INTEGRATION: engine doctor's project scan gains a 'Billboards' section:
'Billboards: N active (M off-screen, K depth-occluded)'
Warning when active count > 50: 'high billboard count — potential perf issue'.

FIRST INTERNAL TEST FIXTURE: a tests/fixtures/billboard scene with three primitives (a box, a sphere, a cylinder) each carrying a Billboard with an 'icon-row' content. Camera orbit. Unit test asserts billboards stay positioned correctly over each anchor as camera moves; off-screen anchors hide their billboards.
PROJECT INTEGRATION SHAPE (forward-looking — first consumer separate story):

Future consumer (Kaboom): replace S150's HUD-side opponent-state strip with billboards. Per bomber, an icon-row billboard with payload.icons derived from BomberStats (shield/pierce/remote/throw-glove). worldOffset = [0, 2.0, 0] (above head height). occlusionMode = 'always-visible' (badges showing through walls intentionally per S150 spec).
Future consumer (Multiplayer): nameplates above each Presence entity. Content: text-line with player name, colour-tinted to recipe palette.
Future consumer (Beacon World): drone status — mini-stat-bar with HP.
None of these projects code is in scope for THIS story — only the engine primitive.
PERFORMANCE BUDGET:
HTML overlay: ~0.1ms per visible billboard per frame for the projection + style write. 50 billboards = ~5ms / frame at worst. Within budget.
Hide-when-offscreen short-circuits most of the work for off-screen billboards.
Depth-test raycast is the expensive bit (~0.5ms per depth-tested billboard). Only enable on the few elements that need it.
DETERMINISM: billboards are PRESENTATION ONLY — no gameplay state touched. Different cameras → different projections, that's fine.
MULTIPLAYER: each client renders its own billboards from the snapshot's entity Transforms + the project-side BomberStats. No protocol changes.
UNIT TESTS:
Anchor entity Transform.position = (5, 1, 0) + worldOffset [0, 1.5, 0] + camera at origin facing -Z → billboard projects to screen-space (5*scale, 2.5*scale) approximately (subject to camera FOV).
Anchor despawn + visibleWhenHidden=false → billboard DOM element removed within 1 frame.
Edge clamp: anchor moves off the right edge of screen + edgeClamp=true → billboard clamps to right edge, hidden when edgeClamp=false.
Scale-with-distance: anchor at distance 5 vs distance 20 → second billboard ~1/4 the pixel size, both within the [min, max] clamp.
Depth-occlusion: anchor behind a hard-block + occlusionMode='depth-tested' → billboard opacity 0.3.
OUT OF SCOPE:
3D-text billboards (text rendered in world space, scaling with perspective). HTML overlay is screen-space-pixels; users wanting in-world text would author their own.
Billboard-to-billboard collision avoidance (nameplates not overlapping each other in a crowd). v1 may overlap; collision-avoidance is a future polish.
Animated billboard content (icons changing over time). Content builders are static per render; project re-registers content on change.
Billboard-as-clickable-DOM (interactive elements above entities). Out — pure display. Click handling is project-side via raycast or HUD-side input.
Mobile / touch optimisations. v1 targets desktop browsers.
